steps.description:
Create a program that asks the user for a positive integer and displays a column of character "#" using the integer as the length.

For example, if the user inputs 3, this will be shown: # # #

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 3

5

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input integer: 3 # # #

Example 2 Input integer: 5 # # # # #

Create a program that asks the user for a positive integer and displays a row of character "#" using the integer as the length.

For example, if the user inputs 3, this will be shown: ###

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - A string can be repeated by an integer. Refer to string operator in notes.

Test Input 3

4

6

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input integer: 3 ###

Example 2 Input integer: 4 ####

Example 3 Input integer: 6 ######

Create a program that asks the user for a positive integer and displays a square with the character "#" using the integer as the length (i.e. number of characters for the row and column).

For example, if the user inputs 3, this will be shown: ### ### ###

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 3

4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input integer: 3 ### ### ###

Example 2 Input integer: 4 #### #### #### ####

Create a program that asks the user for a positive integer and displays a triangle shape with the character "#" using the integer as the number of rows.

For example, if the user inputs 3, this will be shown: # ## ###

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 3

4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input number of rows: 3 # ## ###

Example 2 Input number of rows: 4 # ## ### ####

Create a program that asks the user for 2 positive integers in a row. It will display a line of character "." using the first integer as the length, followed by a line of character "#" using the second integer as the length.

For example, if the user inputs 3 5, this will be shown:

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - Strings can be joined. Refer to string operator in the notes.

Example 1 Input 2 integers: 5 1

Example 2 Input 2 integers: 4 2

Example 3 Input 2 integers: 3 3
